eras.label: The Second Chamber
eras.blurb: The four-estate Riksdag was replaced in 1866 by two chambers, the second of them elected on an income and property qualification that left about a fifth of adult men on the register and a far smaller share actually voting. Turnout below 25% was normal. The Lantmanna Party of the landowning farmers dominated the chamber and the great argument of the period was free trade against protection, which produced two elections in 1887 and settled nothing.

eras.label: The democratic breakthrough
eras.blurb: Proportional representation arrived in 1909 and universal male suffrage with it, and the first PR election in 1911 immediately tripled the Social Democratic vote. The constitutional crisis of 1914 produced two elections in one year, the second of which the Social Democrats won. Parliamentary government was conceded in 1917 and the franchise was extended to women in 1921.

eras.label: Folkhemmet
eras.blurb: The Social Democrats came first at every one of these fourteen elections and governed for all but a handful of the years between them, the longest continuous run of any democratic party in Europe. Per Albin Hansson's phrase for it, the people's home, described a project that ran from pensions and housing to the supplementary pension fight of 1957 to 1960. Turnout climbed from 55% to 89% across the period.

eras.label: One chamber
eras.blurb: The upper house was abolished in 1970 and the whole Riksdag was elected at once, on a four per cent threshold that has shaped Swedish politics ever since. Turnout peaked at 91.8% in 1976, the year the Social Democrats finally lost, and the nuclear referendum and the wage-earner funds dominated the decade that followed.

eras.label: The bloc years
eras.blurb: A banking crisis, an EU referendum and the arrival and departure of New Democracy broke the old five-party arrangement. From 2006 the four centre-right parties campaigned as a single Alliance and won twice, which is the only time the Swedish right has managed consecutive terms.

eras.label: After the Sweden Democrats
eras.blurb: The Sweden Democrats entered the Riksdag in 2010 and every election since has turned on who will and will not deal with them. In 2022 they finished second with 20.5% and supported a government from outside it under a written agreement, the arrangement that ended thirty years of the parties refusing to speak to them.
